title: Third sense: natural as what one has from birth, whether good or not
source_text: XVI. Praeterea naturale significare potest quod cuique inest a nativitate, sive sit naturae bonum atque conveniens, & naturali appetitui consentaneum, sive non. Et ita quoque fatetur primo homini immortalitatem, mortalitatem vero nobis naturalem esse. Ille enim immortalis conditus fuit, nos autem nascimur morti obnoxii.
pass_a_gloss: Further, natural can signify what is in each one from birth, whether it be good and fitting to nature, and agreeable to natural appetite, or not. And thus too he confesses that immortality was natural to the first man, but mortality to us. For he was created immortal, but we are born liable to death.
pass_b_english: Natural can also mean what each person has from birth, whether it is good for nature, suited to it and in keeping with natural appetite, or not. In this sense too, he admits, immortality was natural to the first man and mortality is natural to us. He was created immortal; we are born subject to death.

choices.why: The point is that birth-natural need not be good; the English keeps the either-or in the Latin order.
